log.msg: BEFORE shots: C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Code-lew42-monorepo/c6315543-dde2-46c6-b052-c819794f42e8/scratchpad/shots/before-390.png, before-1280.png, before-3440.png. Verdict: at 3440 the wall used 1450px of 3440 (panel body shrink-wrap beat the width:100% workaround) leaving ~2000px of gutter; at 390 the panel row REFUSED TO STACK, giving the rail 220px of 390 and the wall 155px — one card per row, unusable; 1 card in row 1 (model alone in Read this first) then 3 (Vocabulary), exactly as reported; Stack and Sidebar cards ran 255px tall against a 192px --thumb-max so every row they were in had dead space.

ROOT CAUSES found. (1) The 1-then-3 rows are previews() emitting ONE flat run over 23 children with a full-width heading per group — a 1-member group gets a 1-card row. Fixed by one grid PER BAND. (2) The preview scrollbars are nested scrollers: overflow:hidden already existed on .page-preview-thumb, but the scroller is the .page INSIDE it and a scrollbar is drawn at full size whatever the zoom above it — fixed site-wide with scrollbar-width:none in Page.css. (3) The twin card is 2 device panes at half a card each; a 3440 pane renders at ~0.07x. Fixed in ext/demo/layout.js preview() — twin: still steers the STAGE.

Filter rail verified at 1600: bands Words=6 Pages=6 Apps=11 Reference=6 (29 cards); group filter, search, filtered-to-nothing message and the way back all work; the 6 borrowed word cards point at /flex/gap/ .. /grid/auto/ (real urls, not this page); zero console errors. Search now reads the card MODEL not its textContent, so mail no longer matches Stack and Sidebar.

AFTER shots: C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Code-lew42-monorepo/c6315543-dde2-46c6-b052-c819794f42e8/scratchpad/shots/after-390.png, after-1280.png, after-3440.png, plus C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Code-lew42-monorepo/c6315543-dde2-46c6-b052-c819794f42e8/scratchpad/shots/wall-3440.png (3440x1900, the whole wall in one frame) and the iterations C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Code-lew42-monorepo/c6315543-dde2-46c6-b052-c819794f42e8/scratchpad/shots/try1-3440.png .. try3-3440.png. VERDICT 3440: much better and it looks good — 6 columns, the whole 29-card catalog inside ~1700px so you really do see all the things at once; four bands read as grouped sets; every card is one legible quarter-scale desktop with its footer visible and no scrollbar. The wall now spends 2815px of 3440 (was 1450). STILL WEAK at 3440: the Reference band's four text cards are a third the height of the layout cards, so that row reads light; space/'s card is taller than its five neighbours (fenced, moved to last so it no longer sets the row height from the middle).

VERDICT 1280: clean, 2 columns of ~390px cards, rail 192px sticky. The Words band is the weakest thing at this width — a schematic's boxes are content-sized, so at 390px wide the flex gap card is half empty. That emptiness is literally the lesson (a plain flex gap row does NOT fill its line) and shrinking the track would give 11 near-empty tracks at 3440, so it is left alone. VERDICT 390: fixed and good — the row wraps, rail full-width on top, one full-width card per row at ~358px. Before, it did not wrap at all: the wall got 155px of a 390 screen. Cause was .flex-1 (flex: 1; min-width: 0) shrinking for ever instead of asking for room; layouts.css now declares flex: 1 1 22em, the same declaration sidebar/ spends on its article.

FINDINGS left alone on purpose (in readme Open). (1) stack and sidebar are the two weakest cards and it is the LAYOUT not the preview: .measure carries margin-inline:auto so stack's card is a narrow strip with ~35% empty to its left, and sidebar's body is a readme, so both render as 4px prose with md code fences as black bars. The fix is content (a short designed body like hero/pricing have), which is real work, and a half-redesigned layout is worse than an honestly listed one. (2) space/ card out of family, fenced. (3) doc/file/page.js.md and preview.js.md are stale again and the whole doc/file/ tree is unread — wire it up or delete it. (4) page.js is 147 lines, over RULE#11's 100: five short methods plus trap comments, no second responsibility found worth splitting.

NOT masonry, and that is deliberate. After consolidation every card in a band is the same height, and a masonry wall of uniform children is a grid with extra steps (web.js says the same about notes()); CSS-columns masonry would also put the band headings inside a column and break left-to-right order, and .page-masonry is already a live class in this directory. What Mike asked masonry FOR — see all the things, no gutters at 3440 — is delivered by the dense uniform wall. Revisit if the cards ever go genuinely ragged.
